name: tutorial-steps-visual
description: Step-by-step visual walkthrough of all 23 tutorial steps (0-22) with per-step screenshots for visual regression testing. Exercises the tutorial overlay from start through congratulations, capturing each step's UI state, highlight targets, and progress indicator. Every player-facing step is a real click gated by the tutorial's own rail (issue #479/Finding #74 follow-up), including the box-cut and haul-debris stages the file originally skipped entirely.

expect.note: #553: cash bumped from tutorial_pit's own $80,000 (Level.ts) to $202,824 -- drilling became queued, vehicle-gated work, so this file now pays for a driving_center, a driving.drill_rig course and a tier-1 drill_rig it never used to ($52,780 together), and burns 400 ticks of payroll, fuel and maintenance ($70,044) while the lone driller sinks the 9-hole pattern. The bump is exactly those two, so every cash figure from the drill wait onward is the pre-#553 schedule unchanged. #554: bumped again to $218,824 -- charging is real work too now, and the charge order's own wait step burns more payroll/fuel before the freight_warehouse purchase further down this file, which came up $10,126 short at the old figure. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): bumped once more to $224,000 -- switching the charge-drain wait from chunked tick-N rounds to a single giant tick 225 (see that step's own note, fixing a real interaction-mode deadlock) burns marginally different real fuel/payroll than the chunked version did over the identical 225-tick span, and the freight_warehouse purchase further down came up ~$2,534 short at the old figure. #555 (this merge): bumped again to $300,176 -- dig_ramp_segment is now gated the same way, so this file also needs a driving.excavator course and a rock_digger ($52,500 together) plus the extra payroll/fuel/maintenance drain of the real ticks box-cut now spends actually digging instead of completing in the same tick it was ordered, applied on top of the #554-followup $224,000 baseline; re-verify against an actual run. #556: bumped again, 300176 -> 420176. Every building in this file is queued construction now — the living quarters, the driving centre and the freight warehouse each take real crew time — and the run is ~500 ticks longer end to end as a result. At the old figure the balance went bankrupt while the warehouse was going up, ending the level before the haul and delivery steps this file exists to drive.

steps.description: issue #585: tutorial_start now has a real command-mode implementation too (createRunner.ts), pausing the game the same way the browser boot path (main.ts) always did -- command mode used to report "Unknown command" here and never start anything; now both modes genuinely set state.isPaused = true. The added waitForSelector/waitForTutorialStep only run in interaction mode (command mode has no DOM to wait on) and gate every real click below on the rail actually being armed, mirroring tutorial-interactive.json. #904: the tutorial now opens on hiring (completable immediately, no ticks required) instead of time-speed -- suggesting a faster clock made no sense as the very first card, with an empty site and nothing queued a faster clock would deliver sooner.

Command-mode-only unpause (issue #585): with tutorial_start now genuinely pausing (see its own step above), tickCommand's own loop stops after exactly one real tick while paused regardless of the requested count -- every bare `tick N` below (survey wait, training waits, drill/charge waits, haul wait) would silently advance only 1 tick without this. Interaction mode's own waitForTutorialStep-driven steps run their own real clock independent of console pause state, so this resume has no effect there.

hire-surveyor complete: Crew panel opened, Hire clicked, card advances straight to Survey Terrain. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #923: the speed-control lesson no longer sits here at all -- it moved off this stretch entirely into the box-cut ramp-dig wait further down, so this releases the clock held by tutorial_start's own pause (#585) via advanceToNextStep straight into 'survey'.

Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage: hiring already grants Rookie geology (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts), this only raises the level for tighter survey estimates. No role tag -- there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building, which this scenario does not need.

Target corrected from the file's original x:15 z:15 to x:23 z:23 (Finding #74 follow-up): the tutorial's survey stage gates its picker to REGION.survey, a single exact point at (23,23) (tutorialStages.ts) -- (15,15) is outside that region and the picker would refuse to confirm it under a real click, the same class Finding #42 already found for un-gated drill grids. Result unaffected: nothing downstream reads survey findings by location, only the flat $3,000 survey cost. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern.

Issue #716: replaces the four hand-measured `tick 10` blocks (40 ticks total) this step used to be. The seismic survey ordered above actually completes at tick 14 (direct trace: 'Advanced 10 tick(s). Now at tick 10' then '[tick 14] seismic survey complete'), so 26 of those 40 ticks were pure idle padding with nothing left to wait on -- and idle ticks are not free: the surveyor (employee #1) is the same employee who later becomes the box-cut/drill-plan digger (trained driving.excavator further down), and every idle tick between finishing the survey and being handed a real task drains their hunger/fatigue against SitePolicy's own continuous-mode thresholds (60/60, applied at the set-early-policy step below) with nothing to show for it. Direct trace confirmed this padding was the root cause of #716's box-cut deadlock: with it in place, employee #1 starts the walk to board the rock_digger already below both thresholds, SitePolicy's shouldForceRest fires almost immediately (activeActionId gates it while idle, so this only bites once they're finally given real work), interrupts the walk, and each interruption releases the vehicle reservation (interruptActiveAction, GameLoop.ts) -- forcing a full walk back to re-board on top of the rest itself. The cycle compounds (repeated interruptions crash morale to 0 and fatigue to 100 before a single ramp segment is ever dug), so the box-cut stage's own isComplete (a ramp nav-cell count increasing) never fires within the wait's budget. `waitUntil` on `surveyCount` (mirrors `createComparisonStep`'s own `surveyResults.length` check, tutorialSteps.ts) stops the instant the survey actually lands instead of guessing a fixed tick budget -- matching this file's own #689-followup precedent for the drill/charge waits further down.

toggle-survey-overlay complete (#905): clicking the Survey panel's own overlay-toggle button (#496) — panel is already open from the survey step above — clears the confidence quads and the tutorial card advances to hire-driller.

hire-driller complete: Crew panel opened, Hire clicked. tutorial_start (step 2) arms the tutorial rail (tutorialStages.ts): a control not on the current stage is inert, so every player-facing step below is a real click gated by waitForTutorialStep, matching tutorial-interactive.json's proven pattern. #553: the tutorial no longer goes straight from here to box-cut -- drilling became queued, vehicle-gated work, so the script now teaches the driving_center, the drill_rig licence and the rig itself first. #681: nor does it go straight to that grind any more -- build-living-quarters and set-early-policy land first, protecting the crew before the long stretch that used to run them into a revolt (#586's own fix shrank the drill grid to dodge this; this closes the actual gap.
Test-only bootstrap, not a tutorial stage -- see the geology assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too.

#681: build-living-quarters, click half -- the tutorial's new step 3a-i. Placed right after hiring the driller, before the box-cut/drill-plan/charge/sequence stretch that runs this crew unmanaged for ~400 ticks: a tier-1 living_quarters gives that stretch's forced rest somewhere real to send a collapsing employee, instead of nowhere at all. #556: ordering a building queues a construction site instead of placing it instantly -- this step only confirms the order landed; the wait step right below drives the site to completion, matching tutorial-interactive.json's own equivalent fix.

#556/#816: build-living-quarters complete -- the driller or surveyor (both idle, no skill required for place_building) walks to (18,14) and builds the tier-1 living_quarters. First building of the scenario, so buildingCount settles at exactly 1.

#681: set-early-policy complete -- the tutorial's new step 3a-ii. A living_quarters alone does not force anyone to rest: forceShiftRestIfNeededByPolicy (GameLoop.ts) only engages once state.sitePolicy.revision > 0, so the building from the step above needs this policy applied to actually protect the crew through the grind that follows. Selects Continuous under Shift Mode first, then Apply -- shift_8h's own SHIFT_DURATIONS_TICKS (8) is shorter than a single drill_hole action, so applying it this early interrupted the queued vehicle-gated work below before it could finish (confirmed live pre-#700). Continuous still forces rest on hunger/fatigue (shouldForceRest checks that in every mode), just without the shift-length cap. The later set-policy step (unchanged) still teaches shift_8h once the grind is over.

Hiring a driller grants their 'blasting' qualification, never the driving.drill_rig licence a rig needs, and only a driving_center can teach it. #556/#816: ordering a building queues a construction site instead of placing it instantly, and `employee train` requires a REAL driving_center (state.buildings, not a pending order) -- the wait step right below drives the site to completion before training is attempted, matching tutorial-interactive.json's own equivalent fix.

#556/#816: build-driving-center complete -- the driving_center site finishes construction (root-cause livelock in place_building's dispatch/interruption logic fixed: an idle bystander employee standing on a just-completed building's footprint is now relocated the same way the builder already was, and an idle employee whose own taskQueue holds one permanently-unreachable entry now falls through to the open pool instead of freezing forever).

#553: train-driller, click half -- the course is booked at the driving_center just built. Training takes real ticks (TRAINING_BASE_TICKS, balance.ts), and command mode has no implicit clock between steps, so the wait is the step below. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- living_quarters/driving_center/freight_warehouse all complete for real now that place_building's root-cause dispatch livelock is fixed (tickTaskCompletion.ts relocates a bystander stranded on a just-completed building's footprint; EmployeeDispatchSteps.ts lets an idle employee fall through to the open pool instead of freezing behind one permanently-unreachable queued entry), so this step succeeds genuinely.

#553: train-driller complete -- the course finishes and the driller (employee #2) holds driving.drill_rig. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick.

Training takes real ticks (TRAINING_BASE_TICKS, balance.ts), and command mode has no implicit clock between steps, so the wait is the step below. #816: no longer downstream of the set_policy mode:continuous construction livelock -- living_quarters/driving_center/freight_warehouse all complete for real now that place_building's root-cause dispatch livelock is fixed (tickTaskCompletion.ts relocates a bystander stranded on a just-completed building's footprint; EmployeeDispatchSteps.ts lets an idle employee fall through to the open pool instead of freezing behind one permanently-unreachable queued entry), so this step succeeds genuinely.

#555: train-digger complete -- the course finishes and the surveyor (employee #1) holds driving.excavator. waitForTutorialStep drives the real clock in interaction mode; command mode needs the explicit tick.

#555: buy-rock-digger-assign, first half. Vehicle #2 -- the drill_rig bought above is #1, and the debris_hauler bought further down is therefore #3. #921: a vehicle's driver is claimed automatically now (VehicleReservation/ArrivalGate) -- there is no Assign click and no `vehicle driver` command left to issue, so the purchase itself is the whole step and the tutorial rail advances straight to 'box-cut' on the purchase alone; the newly-licensed digger (employee #1) boards the rock_digger on their own once box-cut's dig_ramp_segment work queues below, with no further player input.

steps.description: #949-followup: added the spacing (3->4, one increment click, 1m/step) and depth (6->8, two increment clicks, 1m/step) stepper clicks before the drag -- both steppers live on the shared ParamStrip (#bs-param-strip-bar, ParamStrip.ts), rendered the instant the grid tool arms, and were unreachable in this step before tutorialStages.ts's own 'drill-plan' stage allowlisted them (defect 2 fix). Without these clicks the drag alone produced a 4x4/spacing:3/depth:6 grid at the panel's own defaults, not the retuned 3x3/spacing:4/depth:8 plan #949 asks for. #553: confirming the 3x3/9-hole grid now only ORDERS the 9 holes -- drill_hole became queued, vehicle-gated work, so they are ghosts until the driller drives the rig to each one, and the tutorial does not advance to `charge` until they have landed. The wait is the step below; the mid-pattern screenshot above is the ghosts-and-real-holes picture #553 asks for. #949: spacing/depth/start retuned from 3/6/(20,20) to 4/8/(22,20), mirroring the exact retune tutorialSteps.ts's own 'drill-plan' stage applies (verified live against the real engine to rate the shot PERFECT with zero casualties/destruction, replacing the old 5m-spacing/8m-depth-at-(20,20) plan that rated CATASTROPHIC). rows/cols/diameter unchanged (still 3/3/0.089). `dragTiles` moved to (22,20)-(30,28) to match the new footprint. KNOWN GAP for the implementer: REGION.drill (tutorialStages.ts) still exact-gates the picker to the OLD (20,20)-(26,26) box (#601-followup, this same file's prior note) -- the tutorial rail itself has to widen/move that region to (22,20)-(30,28) alongside this retune, or a real click-mode drag here rejects every tile outside the stale gate (`.claude/rules/scenario-defs.md`: "pickers reject tiles outside the step's region"). Left for the implementer since tutorialStages.ts is UI rail wiring, not the scripted plan #949 scopes. CI cash mismatch fix (unchanged from the prior pass, still applies): this command carries `diameter:0.089`, the real Drill panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M (Drill.ts) -- an omitted diameter falls back to the console-only 0.15 default and computeDrillHoleDurationTicks (DrillPlan.ts) scales hole duration by diameter, so this keeps command mode's drill_rig busy-time matching a real click's. // TODO(#949): every downstream cash/tick checkpoint through the blast step below was hand-derived against the OLD 3/6/(20,20) plan and needs re-verification against this new 4/8/(22,20) one (different hole spacing changes drill/charge durations, which shifts payroll/fuel drain) -- the implementer/fixer loop verifies live and adjusts the affected `equals`/`decreased`/`note` fields rather than this pass guessing exact figures.

#689-followup: 1/8 of the drill wait, converted from a fixed `tick 50` chunk to a `waitUntil` on holeCount itself. The fixed 8x50=400-tick budget (see this file's own prior #681 note, preserved below on the final chunk) ran to completion regardless of how long drilling actually took -- direct trace against this file's current command sequence (build_ramp/drill_plan exactly as declared, with the current build-living-quarters at 18,14) shows all 9 holes land by tick 216, ~184 ticks earlier than the fixed budget's tick ~400 landing. Those extra ticks were not idle-and-harmless: two employees with nothing to do still drain hunger/fatigue/morale every tick (needsMoraleEffect, EmployeeNeeds.ts), and running ~300 more ticks than necessary before charging even starts was enough on its own to crash wellBeing to 0 and trigger a real worker_revolt at tick 715 -- reproduced identically regardless of living_quarters position (13,4 or 18,14), so the fixed-tick padding itself, not commute distance, was the remaining cause. Stopping the instant holeCount reaches its target removes the wasted ticks; direct trace of the resulting shorter trajectory reaches the charge/sequence/blast stretch below with wellBeing comfortably positive and no revolt.

expect.note: #555 regression guard: the box-cut+drill-plan stretch above is ~250+ ticks of two employees' continuous vehicle-gated work with no living_quarters anywhere in this file's own script -- exactly the pacing that drove wellBeing to a permanent 0 and a worker_revolt game-over here before this fix (ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay had a dead zone at exactly 0: nothing but a strictly positive per-tick delta could ever move a score pinned at the clamped floor, and LevelDef.scoreDecayRate was declared per-level -- tutorial_pit's own 0.01, documented "player-proof" -- but never actually reached updateScores, which always ran the hardcoded global 0.05 instead). Asserting levelEndReason stays null right here, before charge/sequence/blast ever run, is what keeps a future pacing stretch from hiding a revolt behind this file's own closing `campaign complete` debug override again. #681 follow-up: `LevelDef.revoltImmune` (which used to make tutorial_pit immune to worker_revolt outright) is gone -- this block now has to survive the real rules, which is why it is split into eight `tick 50` steps instead of one `tick 400` (see 1/8 above).

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, the same one tutorial-interactive.json carries for the same reason (#707): the surveyor shares the nine charge_hole dispatches with the driller instead of the driller carrying all nine alone. Without it the charge phase runs ~200 ticks with two employees under the continuous policy the tutorial has just taught, well-being reaches zero inside it, and REVOLT_TICKS (120 ticks at zero) then expires during the real construction wait this issue adds below — the level ends in a worker_revolt before the tutorial can finish.

#949: retuned from amount:5 stemming:2 to amount:4 stemming:2.5, mirroring tutorialSteps.ts's own 'charge' stage retune. The click flow now reaches for the amount/stemming steppers explicitly (one decrement click, 5kg->4kg; the amount stepper's step is 1kg, Charge.ts) rather than relying on Charge All at the panel's own 5kg/2m defaults, which is what this step's click sequence used to do when the declared command matched those defaults exactly -- it no longer does. Stemming lands at 2.4m (two increment clicks, 2.0->2.2->2.4; the stemming stepper's own step is 0.2m, Charge.ts) rather than the command's exact 2.5m: the stepper has no way to land on an odd multiple of 0.2 from a 2.0m start, and 2.4m is functionally identical to 2.5m here anyway -- both sit at or above BlastCalc's own full-stemming-effectiveness cap of 0.3x depth (0.3*8=2.4m at this pattern's new depth:8), the same cap this file's own prior note on the buildingCount step below already documents for the old 6m-deep pattern.
